problem.statement: Wrapping a virtualizing WPF ListView in a ScrollViewer (needed for features like zoom/scale) silently disables UI virtualization, turning a 5-second dialog load into a ~60-second one for large datasets.

persona.primary: WPF/.NET developer maintaining a legacy desktop line-of-business application with large data grids

context.situation: A WPF developer building a dialog with a zoom feature needs to nest a large ListView (10,000 rows) inside a ScrollViewer, but this silently disables ListView virtualization.

current_workarounds: Removing the ScrollViewer entirely restores fast load times but sacrifices the desired zoom feature.
Explicitly setting VirtualizingPanel.IsVirtualizing / VirtualizationMode on the ListView (attempted, did not fully resolve the issue since ScrollViewer was still present).

possible_wedges.offer: A XAML/Visual Studio analyzer that statically flags virtualization-breaking patterns (like ScrollViewer wrapping a virtualizing ListView) before the app ships.
A standalone WPF performance audit tool that scans a project's XAML for known virtualization anti-patterns and reports estimated load-time impact.
A drop-in custom Panel/attached-behavior (NuGet package) that lets developers keep zoom/scale features without disabling ListView virtualization.

risks: Single evidence item from one developer; no corroborating reports of prevalence.
Evidence shows near-zero commercial intent (0.05) and no commitment signal (0.0) -- this reads as a free StackOverflow-style question, not a validated willingness to pay.
Very narrow, specific technical edge case; may already have known community fixes (e.g., custom virtualizing panels) that satisfy demand for free.
Unclear whether this pattern is common enough across legacy WPF codebases to justify a dedicated tool versus being a one-off bug.

cheapest_experiment.hypothesis: WPF developers maintaining legacy desktop apps would use a free static XAML checker that flags virtualization-breaking patterns (e.g., ScrollViewer wrapping a virtualizing ListView) if it saves them from ~60s vs ~5s load-time regressions.
cheapest_experiment.input: Post on WPF-focused forums (Stack Overflow answer, r/csharp, WPF Discord) referencing this exact ScrollViewer/virtualization bug, offering a free 'send me your XAML, I'll scan for virtualization anti-patterns' concierge check or a waitlist for an analyzer.
cheapest_experiment.output: Count of developers who submit a XAML file for review or join the waitlist.
cheapest_experiment.commitment_event: A developer submits their XAML file or signs up with their email for early access.
cheapest_experiment.failure_threshold: Fewer than 3 responses after 2 weeks despite multiple forum posts.
